html:
In 1387 the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, the last pagan state in Europe, officially became Catholic Christian.

For two centuries the Lithuanians had kept their own gods while the Teutonic Knights crusaded against them. Christianity came by a marriage deal instead. In the Union of Krewo of 1385, Grand Duke Jogaila agreed to be baptised and to convert his people if he could marry Jadwiga, the young queen of Poland. He was baptised as Władysław in 1386 and crowned king of Poland.

In 1387 he returned to Vilnius, founded a bishopric there and had his subjects baptised in groups. The western region of Samogitia followed only in 1413.

The conversion took away the knights' reason for war, and the joined Polish and Lithuanian forces broke them at Grunwald in 1410. It also began the long partnership that became Poland and Lithuania.
sum: In 1387 the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, the last pagan state in Europe, officially became Catholic Christian.
